questions.q: Acetophenone is treated with (1) HS–CH₂CH₂–SH, H⁺ and then (2) Raney nickel. The final product is:
questions.explain: Step 1 forms a cyclic thioketal and Raney nickel then replaces both C–S bonds by C–H, so C=O becomes CH₂. The overall result is the same as Clemmensen or Wolff–Kishner.

questions.q: A ketone carries groups that are destroyed by both hot concentrated HCl and hot KOH. The best way to convert its C=O into CH₂ is:
questions.explain: The Mozingo route runs under nearly neutral conditions, so it suits substrates sensitive to both acid and base. Clemmensen is strongly acidic, Wolff–Kishner strongly basic, and NaBH₄ stops at the alcohol.

questions.q: Which statement about the Raney nickel step of the Mozingo reduction is correct?
options: Ethane-1,2-dithiol is regenerated and can be reused
The sulfur ends up as nickel sulfide, so a large excess of Raney nickel is needed
Raney nickel only removes one sulfur atom, giving a thiol
The step needs concentrated acid to cleave the C–S bonds
questions.explain: Every C–S bond is cleaved and the sulfur is taken up irreversibly as nickel sulfide, so the dithiol is consumed. Showing the dithiol coming back is the common mistake.

questions.q: Benzaldehyde is treated with ethane-1,2-dithiol and acid, but the Raney nickel step is omitted. The product isolated is:
questions.explain: Without Raney nickel the reaction stops at the cyclic thioacetal, which is simply a protected carbonyl group. Toluene forms only after desulfurisation.
